notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 65-year-old female admitted for upper GI bleed. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.75, creatinine 0.91-0.94, hemoglobin 10.3-12, platelets 264-275, sodium 140-141, wbc 6.7-7.4; vitals dbp 72-75, heart_rate 83-89, map 89-93, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 124-131, spo2 97, temp 36.5-36.8
Day 0 orders/meds/results: EGD: bleeding duodenal ulcer, treated with endoscopic clips; Pantoprazole 80 mg IV
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Acute posthemorrhagic anemia.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.94-0.95, hemoglobin 9.2-10, platelets 266-274, sodium 140-141, wbc 6.9-7.3; vitals dbp 71-77, heart_rate 84-89, map 89-95, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 123-131, spo2 97-98, temp 36.5-36.7
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Transfuse 1 unit packed red blood cells
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Acute posthemorrhagic anemia. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 65-year-old female, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Acute posthemorrhagic anemia. Follow up with primary care in one week. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed.
